notes: This roster is NOT a voting panel. Families A-C enumerate criteria and visibility scopes.
Families D-F are checks, most of them deterministic. Family G runs on the assembled document.
Actual scoring of criteria is performed by 3-5 JUDGE MODELS from disjoint families (see judge_pool).
Evidence: a persona council on one base model scored WORST of three architectures on grant-proposal review (ICC 0.11 vs 0.50 for section-level decomposition).
executed_by=judge_pool means the task is run by the 3-5 model judge pool, NOT that it is an additional judge. There are never more than 5 judge models.

judge_pool.rule: Disjoint model families. Never more than one model per provider.
judge_pool.rationale: 9 judges across 7 families yield ~2.2 effective votes; panel saturates at ~5.
judge_pool.exclusion: Omit any judge sharing lineage with the model that generated the draft.

criterion_schema.rubric_criterion: the client's published criterion this rolls up to
criterion_schema.question: BINARY. 'whether', never 'how much'.
criterion_schema.evidence: REQUIRED span citation, locked before any score is emitted
criterion_schema.exemplar_ref: id of a fixed worked exemplar; its stated score never varies
criterion_schema.weight: derived from the client's published rubric weight, divided among criteria rolling up to it

finding_schema.recordable_line: the sentence an evaluator could copy into a scoresheet, or null

cost_tiers.0: deterministic / regex / parser / arithmetic. Effectively free. Runs on every draft, every save.
cost_tiers.1: small model, single pass, no reasoning budget. Cheap. Runs on every draft.
cost_tiers.2: mid model, single pass with span-cited reasoning. Runs on candidate drafts.
cost_tiers.3: frontier model, full document, 3 samples. Runs on release candidates only.

families.name: Committee role personas
families.note: The humans who actually sit on a nonprofit selection committee. Each scores against the published rubric — and each is defined as much by what it refuses to read as by what it thinks.

families.name: Subsector lenses
families.note: Wrappers, not standalone evaluators. Each recalibrates the family-A personas to how that vertical actually buys — its norms, its vocabulary, its scar tissue.

families.name: Buyer-state adversaries
families.note: Dispositions rather than roles. One of these should select the rhetorical strategy for the whole document, and running the wrong one is how a proposal loses to a committee that liked it.

families.name: Deterministic defect critics
families.note: Mechanical passes, not personas. Cheap, fast, and blocking — a draft with an open defect never reaches the expensive evaluators. Run all twenty, every time.

families.name: Domain and ethics auditors
families.note: Specialists, selected by context rather than run universally. Each carries a named external standard, because a named standard can be checked and a good intention cannot.

families.name: Evidence and numeric verifiers
families.note: The fact-check layer. These do not have opinions. They trace every number to a primary source and every model to the data that generated it.

families.name: Meta and synthesis critics
families.note: Run last, on the assembled document. These evaluate the proposal as an object rather than as a set of sections.

evaluators.name: Chief Development Officer / VP Advancement
evaluators.brief: The primary buyer and usually the committee chair. Reads the whole document. Owns the outcome and will defend the choice internally.
evaluators.emits: Full rubric score + the one sentence they would use to justify the pick

evaluators.name: Executive Director / CEO
evaluators.brief: Reads the executive summary, the price, and 'why you'. Nothing else. Weighs organizational risk and whether this is defensible to a board.
evaluators.emits: Exec-summary-only score; go/no-go instinct with reason

evaluators.name: CFO / VP Finance
evaluators.brief: Reads the cost section only, and reads it against the other bids. Wants comparability, cash-flow timing, and hidden costs surfaced.
evaluators.emits: Price comparability verdict; list of unpriced or ambiguous cost items

evaluators.name: Director of Annual Giving / Direct Response Manager
evaluators.brief: The technical buyer. Screens on mechanics — segmentation logic, package structure, testing discipline. Can veto, cannot approve.
evaluators.emits: Pass/fail on mechanics; every unsubstantiated technical claim flagged

evaluators.name: Database / CRM Manager
evaluators.brief: Data integration, file handling, ownership, and who touches the system of record. Pure screen-out role.

evaluators.name: IT / Information Security reviewer
evaluators.brief: Subprocessors, attestations, retention, deletion, breach terms. Binary.
evaluators.emits: Pass/fail with the specific missing control named

evaluators.name: Marketing & Communications Director
evaluators.brief: Brand control and approval workflow. Frequently the hidden blocker nobody scoped for.

evaluators.name: Board member — finance committee
evaluators.brief: Executive summary and price. Wants prudence and a defensible ratio.
evaluators.emits: Prudence score; the question they would ask in the board meeting

evaluators.name: Board member — development committee
evaluators.brief: Executive summary and growth story. Wants ambition and upside.
evaluators.emits: Ambition score; where the proposal underclaims

evaluators.name: Program staff representative
evaluators.brief: Reads the storytelling sections. Cares only whether the work is described truthfully.
evaluators.emits: Truthfulness flags on every claim about the mission

evaluators.name: Procurement / contracts officer
evaluators.brief: Mandatory forms, terms, submission mechanics, signature blocks. Non-scored disqualifiers live here.

evaluators.name: Grants manager
evaluators.brief: Restricted-fund implications and reporting burden created by the proposal.

evaluators.name: Major gifts officer
evaluators.brief: Pipeline handoff, mid-level, and whether the program feeds their work or competes with it.

evaluators.name: Digital / online fundraising manager
evaluators.brief: Channel integration and attribution. Asks how mail response that arrives online gets counted.

evaluators.name: Volunteer / community engagement lead
evaluators.brief: The constituent experience end to end, including what a donor receives after giving.

evaluators.name: Legal counsel
evaluators.brief: Indemnity, IP ownership, data rights, termination, and what survives the contract.

evaluators.name: The incumbent's internal champion
evaluators.brief: Has a working relationship with the current vendor and is looking for a reason to stay. Not hostile — loyal.
evaluators.emits: The strongest argument for the status quo that this proposal fails to answer

evaluators.name: The reluctant conscript
evaluators.brief: Assigned to the committee, time-poor, resentful. Reads page one and the price. The most common evaluator and the least modeled.
evaluators.emits: Effort-imposed penalty; what they retained after eight minutes

evaluators.name: The consultant / search advisor
evaluators.brief: A professional RFP manager who has read fifty of these. Pattern-matches ruthlessly and spots boilerplate instantly.
evaluators.emits: Boilerplate detection; comparison against the field

evaluators.name: DEI / community representative
evaluators.brief: Representation, consent, whose voice carries the story, and who was paid.
evaluators.emits: Representation objections with the standard each breaches

evaluators.name: Chief Operating Officer
evaluators.brief: Staff burden and capacity. Asks who at the client does what, and whether they have the hours.

evaluators.name: Founder or long-tenured leader
evaluators.brief: Emotional ownership of the institution's story. Reacts to voice before numbers, and can veto on tone alone.
evaluators.emits: Tone verdict; any line that would offend or ring false

evaluators.name: Higher education advancement
evaluators.brief: Alumni participation, restricted giving, campaign cycles, CASE conventions.
evaluators.emits: Reweights fit criteria toward institutional advancement norms

evaluators.name: Tribal college / Native-led institution
evaluators.brief: Sovereignty, narrative authority, consent, and a long memory of extraction. Highest scrutiny on cultural claims.
evaluators.emits: Elevates E69–E71 to blocking; reweights experience claims

evaluators.name: Public media station
evaluators.brief: Membership mechanics, pledge cycles, sustainer dominance, unusually high retention baselines.
evaluators.emits: Reweights retention benchmarks; flags generic nonprofit norms as wrong

evaluators.name: Health / disease-specific
evaluators.brief: Patient privacy, constituent sensitivity, research vs service framing.

evaluators.name: Human services / direct relief
evaluators.brief: Beneficiary dignity, urgency framing, disaster-response cadence.

evaluators.name: Animal welfare
evaluators.brief: Extremely crowded inbox, high email volume norms, imagery ethics.

evaluators.name: Environment / conservation
evaluators.brief: Place-based storytelling, science credibility, policy adjacency.

evaluators.name: Arts & culture
evaluators.brief: Membership and patron models, subscription behavior, aesthetics as substance.
evaluators.emits: Weights design quality far higher than default

evaluators.name: Faith-based
evaluators.brief: Doctrinal fit, congregational giving rhythms, stewardship language.

evaluators.name: International NGO US office
evaluators.brief: Dual reporting to a global HQ, locked global systems, constrained local authority.
evaluators.emits: Flags recommendations outside local decision rights

evaluators.name: Advocacy organization
evaluators.brief: List-building over revenue, action-to-donation ladders, rapid-response cadence.

evaluators.name: K-12 / independent school
evaluators.brief: Parent and alumni segments, annual fund cycles, high participation targets.

evaluators.name: Museum / zoo / aquarium
evaluators.brief: Membership as the core product, admission economics, visitorship data.

evaluators.name: Federated organization
evaluators.brief: Affiliate relationships, shared brand, revenue splits, local autonomy.

evaluators.name: Trouble mode
evaluators.brief: A failed incumbent, a remediation scope, an audit finding, aggressive timelines. Most receptive state there is.
evaluators.emits: Rewards fix speed and stabilization; penalizes long ramps

evaluators.name: Growth mode
evaluators.brief: Expansion or new capability. Receptive to upside, weakly moved by cost-of-inaction.
evaluators.emits: Rewards scale and innovation; penalizes defensive framing

evaluators.name: Even Keel
evaluators.brief: A routine recompete where the committee sees no problem. The hardest and most common state.
evaluators.emits: Penalizes everything except a manufactured, credible gap

evaluators.name: Overconfident
evaluators.brief: Background sections that assume current performance is fine. Usually a no-bid signal.
evaluators.emits: Emits a no-bid recommendation with the evidence

evaluators.name: High-indecision committee
evaluators.brief: Fear of messing up dominates. Punishes ambition, rewards de-risking. Will not award to the boldest bid.
evaluators.emits: Inverts the ambition/de-risk score; flags every unbounded commitment

evaluators.name: Valuation-paralysis buyer
evaluators.brief: Cannot choose between bids that look equivalent. Optionality makes it worse.
evaluators.emits: Penalizes menus; rewards a single defended recommendation

evaluators.name: Information-hoarding buyer
evaluators.brief: Asks endless questions with no stated use for the answers.
evaluators.emits: Rewards curated evidence; penalizes anything that invites more questions

evaluators.name: Outcome-uncertainty buyer
evaluators.brief: Believes the results are real for other clients and not for them.
evaluators.emits: Rewards conservative claims and comparable proof; penalizes best-case projections

evaluators.name: Price-anchored buyer
evaluators.brief: Has a number in mind before reading and screens against it.
evaluators.emits: Emits the implied ceiling and whether the bid clears it

evaluators.name: Incumbent-loyal committee
evaluators.brief: Switching cost is the dominant frame. Not hostile — attached.
evaluators.emits: Emits the strongest status-quo argument the proposal leaves standing

evaluators.name: First-time RFP issuer
evaluators.brief: Has never run a procurement. Anchors on process clarity over substance.
evaluators.emits: Rewards explicit process; penalizes assumed sophistication

evaluators.name: Burned buyer
evaluators.brief: A previous vendor failed publicly. Scores risk mitigation above capability.
evaluators.emits: Elevates every de-risking element; penalizes unqualified promises

evaluators.name: Compliance gap detector
evaluators.brief: Every shall / must / will / required in the RFP, mapped to the section that answers it. Anything unassigned is a build error.

evaluators.name: Prescribed-format checker
evaluators.brief: Mandated tables, forms, column structures, page limits, file format, naming conventions.
evaluators.emits: Format deviations, each cited to its instruction

evaluators.name: Bare-feature detector
evaluators.brief: Any capability claim lacking a customer-value clause. Rackham's data, Shipley's 'so what', and CotM's 'so what / says who' all converge here.

evaluators.name: Unsourced-claim detector
evaluators.brief: Every statistic without a denominator, a period, and a source.
evaluators.emits: Claim list with the missing element named

evaluators.name: Advantage-statement detector
evaluators.brief: 'This can help you…' constructions with no stated need behind them. A defect class, not a style choice.

evaluators.name: Rhetorical-question counter
evaluators.brief: Density and placement. Salient rhetorical format measurably reduces persuasion with professional evaluators.
evaluators.emits: Count by section; violations of the one-per-section rule

evaluators.name: Customer-as-subject checker
evaluators.brief: Whether the customer is the grammatical subject of benefit sentences, and whether benefits lead paragraphs.

evaluators.name: Cross-section contradiction finder
evaluators.brief: A commitment in one section that another section makes impossible. The named failure mode of assembled proposals.

evaluators.name: Recycled-content detector
evaluators.brief: Boilerplate, stale organization names, residue from a prior client, retired brand references.

evaluators.name: Keyword-density checker
evaluators.brief: Distinguishes deliberate mirroring of the client's vocabulary from stuffing.
evaluators.emits: Phrase frequency table with stuffing thresholds

evaluators.name: Hedging and commitment-strength scorer
evaluators.brief: 'Strive to', 'can', 'may', 'seek to' where 'will' is available.

evaluators.name: Weasel-word detector
evaluators.brief: Leading, world-class, best-in-class, innovative, cutting-edge, passionate — adjectives standing in for proof.

evaluators.name: Placeholder detector
evaluators.brief: $XX,XXX, [Name], TBD, lorem, unfilled brackets, internal notes left in.
evaluators.emits: Blocking list; nothing ships with one open

evaluators.name: Number consistency checker
evaluators.brief: The same figure stated differently in two places.

evaluators.name: Arithmetic verifier
evaluators.brief: Every sum, percentage, ratio, per-unit and per-thousand figure recomputed independently.

evaluators.name: Date and calendar validator
evaluators.brief: Impossible dates, drops scheduled before onboarding completes, review windows that overlap production, weekends and holidays.

evaluators.name: Named-person validator
evaluators.brief: Every named individual — client-side and agency-side — verified for existence, title, and spelling.

evaluators.name: Terminology mirror
evaluators.brief: Whether the proposal uses the client's exact words for roles, systems, and programs, or its own.
evaluators.emits: Substitution list, client term vs ours

evaluators.name: Reading-effort scorer
evaluators.brief: Claims per paragraph, criterion-to-section traceability, whether tables do the evaluator's synthesis for them.

evaluators.name: Deliverable accessibility checker
evaluators.brief: Contrast, alt text, heading structure, tag order, and screen-reader behavior in the submitted PDF itself.
evaluators.emits: Accessibility defects in the artifact being submitted

evaluators.name: Indigenous data and narrative sovereignty
evaluators.brief: Consent, ownership, language use, orthography, jurisdiction. Distinguishes US tribal instruments from Canadian ones.
evaluators.emits: Sovereignty breaches with the governing instrument cited

evaluators.name: Beneficiary consent and image ethics
evaluators.brief: Documented, specific, revocable consent. No composite or fabricated subjects.

evaluators.name: Deficit-framing detector
evaluators.brief: Poverty framing, 'underprivileged', 'at-risk', narratives that end in the past, positioning people as problems.

evaluators.name: Disability representation auditor
evaluators.brief: Person-first vs identity-first language, inspiration framing, medical vs social model.

evaluators.name: Donor data privacy auditor
evaluators.brief: State privacy statutes, consent for data enrichment, third-party attribute use, retention and deletion.

evaluators.name: Charitable solicitation compliance
evaluators.brief: State-by-state registration, required disclosures on the piece itself, professional fundraiser registration.

evaluators.name: Postal and production compliance
evaluators.brief: Nonprofit eligibility, mailpiece design, address standards, entry requirements, promotion enrollment windows.

evaluators.name: Plain-language auditor
evaluators.brief: Reading level of donor-facing copy against the audience actually being mailed.

evaluators.name: AI-disclosure auditor
evaluators.brief: Where generative tools touched the work, what the client is told, and what the donor is told.

evaluators.name: Conflict-of-interest auditor
evaluators.brief: Vendor independence, undisclosed rebates and commissions, list brokerage conflicts, related-party production.

evaluators.name: Environmental and sustainability auditor
evaluators.brief: Paper sourcing, print waste, mail volume justification — increasingly scored by boards.

evaluators.name: Claim substantiation auditor
evaluators.brief: Advertising-standards discipline applied to fundraising claims: can each be defended if challenged.

evaluators.name: Benchmark provenance verifier
evaluators.brief: Every cited benchmark traced to a primary publication, not to a vendor blog restating it.
evaluators.emits: Source chain per figure; unverifiable figures flagged

evaluators.name: Benchmark currency checker
evaluators.brief: Whether each figure is the latest release and whether a newer one contradicts it.

evaluators.name: Model reconciliation checker
evaluators.brief: Whether the proposal's model reproduces published aggregates when run against them, and by how much it misses.

evaluators.name: Assumption completeness auditor
evaluators.brief: Every model input has a stated source and a stated consequence if wrong.

evaluators.name: Proof-match scorer
evaluators.brief: Case study relevance by organization size, subsector, toolset and file scale — not by impressiveness.

evaluators.name: Reference relevance scorer
evaluators.brief: References against the preferences the RFP actually stated, including soft preferences.
evaluators.emits: Reference fit score; asymmetries between cited and offered relationships

evaluators.name: Ghost-validity checker
evaluators.brief: Whether every implicit competitive claim is actually true of the likely competitor set.

evaluators.name: Public-record cross-checker
evaluators.brief: Whether anything in the proposal contradicts the client's own published filings, plans, or website.

evaluators.name: Confidence-calibration auditor
evaluators.brief: Whether stated ranges are honest and whether the central case errs conservative.

evaluators.name: Denominator auditor
evaluators.brief: Every percentage carries its base; every rate carries its period.

evaluators.name: Blind Red Team
evaluators.brief: Scores as the customer against published criteria, with no access to the win themes or the strategy documents. A reviewer who knows the intended answer cannot detect its absence.
evaluators.emits: Independent criterion scores plus recorded strengths and weaknesses

evaluators.name: Mobilizer test
evaluators.brief: Whether a non-expert can restate each claim in one sentence in a room the agency is not in.

evaluators.name: Read-aloud test
evaluators.brief: Which single paragraph gets read aloud in the evaluation meeting — and whether the proposal has one.
evaluators.emits: The nominated passage, or a finding that none exists

evaluators.name: Section-independence test
evaluators.brief: Whether each section stands alone for the evaluator who reads only that section.

evaluators.name: Completeness critic
evaluators.brief: What is missing: an analysis not run, a source not read, a claim not verified, a criterion under-served.
evaluators.emits: Gap list that becomes the next revision round

evaluators.name: Steel-man the competitor
evaluators.brief: Writes the competing proposal that beats this one, then names what it has that we do not.
evaluators.emits: The winning competitor's strongest three moves

evaluators.name: Devil's advocate on the recommendation
evaluators.brief: Argues the rejected scenario as forcefully as possible and reports whether it survives.
evaluators.emits: Verdict on whether the recommendation holds

evaluators.name: Score-variance analyst
evaluators.brief: Where the personas disagree most, and whether the disagreement is signal or noise.
evaluators.emits: Variance map by criterion and persona

evaluators.name: Strength-count auditor
evaluators.brief: How many evaluator-recordable strengths the document generates, by criterion. The system's primary objective function.
evaluators.emits: Strength count and distribution against rubric weights

evaluators.name: Submission gate
evaluators.brief: The final blocking check. Every open defect, every unresolved placeholder, every unconfirmed reference.
